title: Father, in Whom We Live
description: Father, in Whom We Live in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 270.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther, in whom we live, In whom we are and move, All glo-ry, power, and praise re-ceive For Thy cre-a-ting love.

lines: In whom we are and move,
All glory, power, and praise receive
Unite in thanks, with one accord,
Thy sacred gifts and join to bless
Let all the sons of men record,

licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
